$comment: Machine-readable adopter-side configuration. Human-readable twin: docs/PORTING.md. Keep the two in sync — verify_citations.py check 2 reads this file to detect defaults that were never substituted.

$kinds.default: Has a working default. Change it only if your repo already uses a different name.
$kinds.detected: Determined by running a command at install time. Never write a literal for these.
$kinds.required: No sensible default exists. The installer must ask, or the feature degrades visibly.
$kinds.optional: Safe to leave empty. The dependent feature turns itself off rather than failing.

rules_doc.description: The always-loaded rules document for your repo. Every skill cites it.

backlog_file.description: Open and actionable items only. Resolved entries move to archive_file.

archive_file.description: Resolved history with citations. Never read by default.

mistakes_file.description: Process mistakes — how work was done wrongly, not what is broken in the code.

design_docs_dir.description: Where spec saves design documents. A trailing slash is expected. If your path contains a space, keep it quoted everywhere it appears in a shell command.

notes_file_pattern.description: Companion notes file naming. The literal token {tool} is replaced with the component's own name. Use '{tool}/NOTES.md' instead if you prefer notes inside each component's folder.

checklist_section.description: Heading text of the backlog section implement-queue reads as its work queue.

default_branch.description: Your repo's default branch. NEVER hardcode this — 'main' and 'master' are both common and getting it wrong silently targets a branch that does not exist.

detect.note: Preferred. Outputs 'origin/<branch>' — strip the 'origin/' prefix. Fails if the repo has no remote, or if origin/HEAD was never set (common in a clone made with --single-branch); 'git remote set-head origin --auto' fixes the latter.
Fallback. Reports the CURRENTLY checked-out branch, which is only the default branch if that is what happens to be checked out. Confirm with the user rather than assuming.

python_cmd.description: Interpreter used by the hook scripts.

detect.note: Preferred. IMPORTANT: test that it actually RUNS, as shown — do not use 'command -v python3'. On Windows, 'python3' is frequently a Microsoft Store stub that resolves successfully on PATH and then fails on execution, so a resolve-only check picks a broken interpreter and reports success.
Fallback, and the working interpreter on most Windows installs. Same rule: verify execution, not resolution.

test_command.description: How to run your test suite. Cited by the code-reviewer agent so it can re-run tests rather than reasoning about whether they would pass. No default is provided on purpose — a wrong test command produces a review that silently never tests anything. If your repo genuinely has no test suite yet, the installer records this value's source as 'confirmed_none' rather than 'left_empty' — a deliberate, informed answer, distinct from the question simply not being answered yet. code-reviewer must then state plainly in its output that no automated tests were run, rather than either fabricating a command or silently reporting clean with nothing actually checked.

lint_command.description: Linter for .githooks/pre-commit. Invoked from a scratch directory with staged file paths appended, so a bare relative path to a linter binary will not resolve — use $REPO_ROOT, which the hook pre-sets. Empty disables the lint step entirely, which is the shipped default.

flagged_surfaces.description: Specific functions, files, or modules in YOUR codebase with a documented history of subtle bugs. A change that would otherwise be Tier 4 gets the full QA gate if it touches one. Ships empty because this is a property of your code. Grow it reactively: add a place when a subtle bug turns out to be in the same place as a previous subtle bug. Keep it short — a list of twenty escalates everything and therefore escalates nothing.

available_models.description: Which Claude models you have access to, ordered weakest-to-strongest, so 'the strongest model you have' has an actual answer: the last entry in this list. Paired with fable_available below.

fable_available.description: Reversed 2026-09-05 (the two-axis SDLC redesign) — this used to be review_model_families, whose rule was 'if only one family is available, skip the review VISIBLY rather than running a same-family pass and calling it cross-model.' That's no longer the rule: the review always runs, on a fresh context on the most different model you have, in preference order — Fable when this flag is true; otherwise another Claude model (checked against available_models above: sonnet-/haiku-drafted reviews on opus, opus-drafted reviews on sonnet); only when nothing else is reachable at all does it fall back to the same model in a fresh context. The heading names the actual reviewing model every time (e.g. '## Design review — Opus, fresh context') and never claims more independence than that pass actually had. Skipping is no longer an option in any case — a same-model pass, correctly labeled, is preferred over silently skipping.

subagent_models.description: Default model per bundled subagent. docs-writer is mechanical transcription and runs well on the cheapest tier; code-reviewer needs real reasoning. Override per-call when a specific pass warrants it — a review of code that will run on someone else's machine is worth a stronger, different-family model.
